All three solver paths work. Here's what changed and why:

**`@FunctionalInterface MstSolver`** — a single-method interface with `List<Edge> solve(Graph graph)`. The annotation is a compile-time guard: it prevents accidentally adding a second abstract method, which would silently break all lambda usages.

**`KruskalSolver implements MstSolver`** — no behavior changes; `solve` just gains `public @Override`. Because it now satisfies the SAM contract, any `KruskalSolver` can be passed wherever `MstSolver` is expected without casting.

**`runAndPrint(String, MstSolver, Graph)`** — the injection point. It accepts `MstSolver` by interface type, so `KruskalSolver` instances, lambdas, and any future implementation all flow through the same method without overloading or branching.

**`heaviestEdge` lambda** — a one-liner `MstSolver` defined inline with no named class. It demonstrates that callers can supply ad-hoc solving logic (useful in tests or one-off analyses) without implementing `KruskalSolver`'s full configuration.
